title.narrative: Strengthened institutional capacity of workers' organizations

description.narrative: Cognizant of the challenge posed by climate change on the people of Somalia that is characterised by prolonged floods and droughts that have led to unprecedented humanitarian disasters, the constituents of Somalia requested ILO’s support to find sustainable measures to overcome the challenges. The disastrous effects induced by climate change in the specific context of Somali working families include the loss of livelihoods, the decrease in decent work opportunities and an alarming increase in the number of internally displaced people - a key driver of insecurity. By 2030, Somalia is expected to lose more than 5 per cent of its total working hours (equivalent to around 172,000 full-time jobs) due to climate-related heat stress. These trends are likely to intensify in the future unless coherent policies and response measures are put in place to facilitate the transition to a low-carbon economy. However, the adaptation and mitigation targets contained in Somalia's National Adaptation Strategy, although ambitious, are still far below the standards set and defined by the Paris, Glasgow, and Sharm El Sheikh COP agreements. In view of the above, it is imperative that Somali workers and their trade union representatives acting under the aegis of the Federation of Somali Trade Unions (FESTU) gain not only a better understanding of the implications of climate change for the world of work, but also build the necessary capacities that would enable them to become powerful advocates and agents of change towards job-rich green growth and an environment-friendly agenda based on the cardinal principles of just transition and decent work. The intervention under the CPO SOM802 aims to bolster the capacity of ILO constituents, particularly the Federation of Somalia Trade Unions (FESTU) and its affiliates, to advocate for workers' rights in the charcoal industry, promote fair working conditions, and explore alternative livelihood opportunities.
